runnerCompletedDefinition: every recorded item was processed; false when any item stayed not-run. It says nothing about whether the observations passed.
compatibilityMetDefinition: official mode only, and every required observation is confirmed. A required item that is limited, unavailable, not-run, or failed keeps it false; a fixture run is always false, and so is a run on a substituted host, which is never the fixed official artifact. It does not certify migration or deleting the fork: the base spec keeps the existing agent dir write-back and persistent settings write unproven, and those stay outside the required list. It also says nothing about whether role, /clear, or /model is available: the matrix item is confirmed as soon as any purpose is observed, so read its observed purpose count instead.

results.detail: confirmed here means observed on the dedicated Pi, including 0 purpose(s) observed as unavailable; 11 of 13 purposes observed, rows derive from those observations

data.confirmedMeans: a purpose behaviour was observed on the dedicated Pi; unavailable is an observation too

rows.purpose: Route review/deep work to strong while keeping one selection
rows.alternative: The same extension routing; the route reports its role to the extension status line
rows.difference: No /model role suffix or core footer badge; the routing decision itself is identical

rows.purpose: Pin normal or strong without changing the model
rows.alternative: /spirits-role <role>: locks the phase, records a spirits_role entry, writes models.role
rows.difference: A separate command; pi's /model keeps its own behaviour, and the lock survives resume and reload

rows.purpose: Show which role handled the last request
rows.currentMechanism: Core footer badge reading the route role
rows.alternative: ui.setStatus() on the extension status line, updated by the route
rows.difference: Renders on the footer's extension status line, not beside the model name

rows.purpose: Set the role and thinking level of one workflow step
rows.difference: The step list decides which names exist; an unknown name is ignored and reported by /spirits-role status

rows.purpose: Read how the routing is running: the lock, the step, and both roles' targets
rows.alternative: /spirits-role status: one report listing the routing state, the lock, the running step, the last request, and what each role resolves to
rows.difference: pi shows a selection, never a routing: this report is the only surface that names the target a role answered with

rows.purpose: Remove conversation from context while the display keeps it
rows.alternative: /spirits-clear: a boundary entry plus a context handler that drops what precedes it
rows.difference: The chat display keeps the earlier messages; pi's /clear removes them from the display too

rows.purpose: Keep the same session ID after clearing
rows.currentMechanism: Core clearConversation() keeps the session file and ID
rows.alternative: /spirits-clear appends one entry and rewrites nothing
rows.difference: None for the ID; the session file keeps growing instead of being reset

rows.purpose: Keep the TODO list after clearing
rows.currentMechanism: TODO snapshots live outside the cleared conversation
rows.alternative: Same: the boundary is a conversation cut, not a session reset
rows.difference: None; a new session would drop the TODO list

rows.alternative: /spirits-role <role> thinking <level>: a per-role setting the route puts on the request, measured in the fake provider's request body
rows.difference: The setting belongs to the role, not to the session; pi's own set_thinking_level still owns the session selection and spirits never calls it

rows.purpose: Give one role its own model and save it
rows.currentMechanism: Core /model parser and default save keys
rows.alternative: /spirits-role <role> model <ref>: a merge-write of models.<role> into pi's global settings.json, under pi's file lock, read back after the reload
rows.difference: The selection is the target of a role, not the session's model; pi's own selection stays where /model put it

rows.purpose: Choose the session's model and read the choice back
rows.currentMechanism: Core /model selector and the session model it saves
rows.alternative: pi's own set_model RPC read back with the session state; spirits routes requests and never selects the session's model
rows.difference: The routing model is one of the choices: selecting it puts every request through the routing, and selecting a physical model takes them out of it

rows.purpose: Save the chosen model and level as defaults
rows.difference: The selector's default save is a terminal surface with no RPC command, so this row is not-run; the session's model selection itself is observable with set_model

rows.purpose: Edit the role settings from an interactive list
rows.alternative: /spirits-role with no arguments opens the list, which exists only in the interactive TUI
rows.difference: The RPC path cannot open a terminal widget, so this row is not-run; every setting the list edits is reachable as a /spirits-role command line
